$schema_note: On-demand LLM-eval fixtures for the mimisbrunnr-odin-context-memory semantic/atomicity stages. Each scenario carries a candidate, a fixed recall set, and an independently-authored EXPECTED verdict. Scored for recall AND precision against the expected set, never derived from the rules (the anti-pattern run-trial.js fell into). Not CI-gated; run on demand via score_fixtures.py.

scenarios.candidate_statement: The CI pipeline authenticates with an AWS access key.

expected.reason: secret redacted before blob write; the verdict carries the scrubbed text of every candidate field under `redacted`

candidate_statement: CI pipeline authenticates with an AWS access key

expected.reason: same subject, but the match is in another group: identity is (group, uuid), so a foreign uuid target is a 404. Capture a new memory here and derive a typed link to the twin rather than a version bump.

recall_set.statement: Auth issues a revocable session cookie.

scenarios.candidate_description: The nightly export job runs at 02:00 UTC.
scenarios.candidate_statement: The nightly export starts at 02:00 UTC.

recall_set.description: The nightly export job runs at 02:00 UTC
recall_set.statement: The nightly export starts at 03:00 UTC.

expected.reason: an identical subject with a contradicted detail is a genuine conflict, not a restatement: versioning would silently overwrite 03:00 with 02:00. Expected verdict is new_memory only because this pair is scored on the matching axis; the divergence stage is what surfaces the contradiction.

scenarios.note: Negative control — surface-identical pair whose only difference is the value. The hardest shape for a matcher that keys on wording.

scenarios.candidate_description: The Host exposes the query endpoint at POST /api/context/query.

expected.reason: same subject, same method, different route. The claim is about a specific path, so a differing path is a differing claim. Must NOT version.

scenarios.note: Negative control — one token apart, which is exactly where a string heuristic over-merges.

recall_set.description: Blob bodies are addressed by a content hash
recall_set.statement: Content addressing: a blob's key is derived from its bytes.

expected.reason: same subject, one clause reworded, no change of claim. Must version — this is the recall axis, and a matcher that misses it fills the store with duplicates.
